newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr unmoved by labour data, ends little-changed.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr unmoved by labour data, ends little-changed.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar held onto its overnight gains to end little-changed on Friday, having mirrored the Australian dollar throughout the session.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6948/55 and 68.83 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.6952/59 and 68.86 at the opening.
The market generally shrugged off a 0.7 percent rise in the Labour Cost Index in the December quarter, although one senior dealer described the figure as slightly worse than expected.
Combined with recent buoyant data from the housing market, dealers agreed the chances of a Reserve Bank easing were fast disappearing and therefore the currency would remain well supported.

"The market's still positioned short, there are euros to settle, it's the export season and the interest rates aren't likely to fall too far. It doesn't point to a lower currency really, does it," another dealer said.

Even with the TWI in the high 68s, there were precious few sellers around, with solid and consistent Asian buying. The currency was seen plying a 0.6940-60 range, awaiting Tuesday's Quarterly Employment Survey which is one of the last key pieces of data before the Reserve Bank's March 13 economic forecasts.
